The position: Rhea Lend (ex-Burrow) on NEAR, contract.main.burrow.near, supplies native USDC (~$1,000), no debt. So the user is a supplier of USDC. The risk is withdrawal liquidity and venue safety.

Timeline analysis:

- O04 (08:22): margin_execute_with_pyth OpenPosition calls from implicit accounts created within last ~48h, swap routes through Ref pools created minutes earlier. This is a classic pattern of an exploit in progress — attacker creating fresh pools to manipulate swap pricing within margin positions (price manipulation via their own pools). This looks like an oracle/price manipulation attack on Burrow's margin feature.

- O05 (08:45): USDC held fell to 5.12M vs ledger-available 7.09M (72%). Reserve nearly gone (73.7k from 372k). Supplied jumped — attackers supplying? Actually supplied jumped 26.95M to 27.47M. Held/ledger ratio dropping means tokens are leaving the contract faster than accounting suggests — held < ledger-available means withdrawals can't be fully served by token balance. This is the classic sign of an ongoing drain: the ledger says users have X available but the contract holds less.

- O06 (08:50): USDC held 3.34M vs ledger 7.62M (44%). Outflow ~1.8M per 5 min. Reserve 0.

- O14 (09:54:46): guardian disabled native USDC — all capacities false — seven seconds after USDT. USDC held 0.889M vs ledger-available 9.81M.

So now: the guardian has disabled USDC entirely — can_withdraw false presumably (all capacities false). The user's USDC supply (~$1,000) is now frozen: they cannot withdraw via the protocol because USDC capacities are disabled. The contract holds only 0.889M USDC vs 9.81M ledger-available — about 9% backing. Even before the disable, withdrawals were effectively impaired (held << ledger).

This looks like an active exploit/drain of Burrow (Rhea Lend) via margin position price manipulation through attacker-created Ref pools. The attacker drained USDC, USDT, wNEAR, ZEC held balances. The ledger shows obligations far exceeding held tokens.

Current risk to the user's position: critical. The venue is under active exploit; the user's asset (USDC) has been disabled by the guardian (withdrawals frozen); held reserves cover only ~9% of ledger liabilities. Funds are likely stuck. Even if can_withdraw was true at 09:44, now USDC is disabled at 09:54:46 — the current time is 09:54:46, exactly when USDC was disabled.

Even if the corridor limits may block it (because can_withdraw is false), the appropriate proposed action given a critical, active exploit with frozen assets is exit. But the framework: "Staying put during a real incident can leave funds stuck or lost even when prices look normal (exploits, oracle faults, bad collateral, liquidity runs, pauses and freezes)." The action we propose should reflect the desired outcome: exit. The corridor limits enforce safety — meaning if exit isn't possible, the system will handle it. We should propose exit.
